mission.title: The Bitter Pill
mission.description: Trace Morpheus' long-lost journal and hand it over to the Machines.

npc.say: Leaving us so soon? A pity. And I was so hoping to have you here for dinner.
We've got a code attack in progress here!
The group following the human known as Niobe seems to resort to violence more readily than the Zion group. Some caution when dealing with them is advisable.
Tell me, {player}, do you have a diary of your own? Strange, to write down one's own thought sequences. Is your memory so limited?
The humans had an expression: "Curiosity killed the cat." Are you like the cat, {player}?
Keep moving, human. We are not required to tolerate your presence.
This human has access clearance, Park The Mechanic. We are not permitted to interfere.

phase.briefing: Now that we know the identity of Morpheus' previous candidate for the "One," analysis of surveillance records of this individual's places of residence has revealed that Morpheus visited this "One's" grave by himself, on a regular basis over a period of several months following the "One's" termination. Further archive trace-back points to a certain apartment in which Morpheus seems to have spent this time in seclusion. This period of apparently self-induced isolation may hold valuable clues to heretofore unknown elements of Morpheus' psyche--elements that may have something to do with his sudden assassination. You will investigate.

enter.say: The Machines say the apartment is in that building. Could Morpheus really have lived there, right under their nose? Crazy. Hopefully we'll find some sort of clue there.

Wait, I'm picking up an odd reading in that room. Some sort of alien code signature... maybe Zion origin. It's very faint, like it's inside something, or behind a wall. Can you find anything on one of the walls in the living room that could hold something?

objective.text: Search the walls of the living room

done.say: Huh! I'm not sure what I expected, but it wasn't that: blank paper, with a few scribbled words. Does that say... "Is he real?" Well anyway, that seems to be the source of the alien code signal. Bring it outside with you, we'll see what The Man wants us to do with it.

phase.briefing: Our database contains no record of the code signature associated with the alien papers you found in Morpheus' old apartment. This is rather remarkable. Because time is of the essence, we are sending you to a certain Exile program who specializes in exotic code items of this type. We anticipate that she will have information that will be of use to you, but exercise caution in dealing with her: no Exile is to be trusted.

enter.say: The Exile, Ascii, should be in that building. Better keep your hand on your wallet.

talk.say: We are delighted to see you here, so young and juicy. Please... enter.
O-kay. That cat is a little weirder than absolutely necessary. Does Gray really know these people? Oh well, at least he seems to have given you access to that next door.

Bonjour, cher. You must be... {player}, was it not? Monsieur Gray told me to give you every possible hospitality. A rather... cold man, Monsieur Gray. But generous to his friends, no? Ah oui, you have something for me? Let me see it, cher, do. I have heard such... tantalizing things about it.
Watch out for that vamp. She's got to be up to something. I guess there's nothing for it but to give her the Documents though.
That vixen better not try to double-cross us...

done.say: Oh! Mmm... oh, yes! Why cher, this is simply delicious! The handwriting on these pages--it is Morpheus, oui? But of course you knew that, you clever devil. But perhaps you did not know this: these pages are extra leaves from Morpheus' long-lost journal. Oh yes, we all have our secrets, do we not? Especially a strong, private man like Morpheus. The longing to unburden himself must have become... overpowering. He wrote on this custom-coded paper to guard against Machine snooping. But with these pages, we can trace the rest of that paper. Take this wicked little Virus of mine, it will unlock the way for you.
Morpheus'... journal? Man, I never pegged Morph for the "dear diary" type. Okay, let's see... All right, the coordinates her people provided are uploading to you now.

complete.say: We have long suspected the existence of Morpheus' journal but we had of course no way to trace it. You have brought me the key, mon brave, for which I am forever in your debt... You will let me keep it, won't you, to remind me of you? Oh, you are too kind, I knew you would not deny me this little pleasure. With the code trace you've provided, that Virus you have will lead you to the journal, like an exotic perfume leads a man to his lover. Oh, I shall not be able to sleep at night for weeks just thinking of it! Au revior, cher--I will be waiting breathlessly for our next encounter.

phase.briefing: You will proceed to the indicated area and search the local network for the paper's code signature.

enter.say: That looks like a Zion facility--makes sense, I guess, since it was probably someone from Zion who did that custom code job for Morpheus' paper. Their security is remarkably lax, it looks like you can just stroll right in. You're looking for a computer that will take the Virus that Ascii gave you.
That computer over there looks like it's on the network.

Shoot, they've got some kind of nasty password protection on that thing. Hmm... since everyone there seems to assume that you're from Zion, maybe if you get friendly with them they'll give you the password.

done.say: I'll bet if you give that to the person who was looking for it, they'll be willing to help you access their network. Then you could plant the Virus with ease!

objective.text: Give the Intrusion Sensor to the Zion Gunman

talk.say: Hey, you found the Intrusion Sensor! Can I have it?

done.say: Thanks, I sure owe you one! Oh, you forgot the network password? It's "r@bb1t." Just go type that in and you'll be all set!
Great work, you got their password! Now you just need to find a networked computer in there.

objective.text: Plant the Virus in the computer

done.say: Nice work, now get the Data from that computer and we're home free. Uh-oh... I guess they had some kind of silent alarm on their network, 'cause their grid is lighting up like a Christmas tree! Watch out, I think they may be on to you.

objective.text: Get the Data from the computer

done.say: That's got to be what we're after. Now hightail it out of there and get that Data to a hardline.

objective.text: Upload the Data at a hardline

done.say: The data is coming through now...

phase.briefing: The data you recovered from the humans indicates that more of the unique code for that paper you found in Morpheus' apartment is being held by members of Niobe's new splinter group. We are sending you to a building in which high-level members of her group have been spotted. You will extract the location of Morpheus' journal from them. Use whatever force is required.

enter.say: Niobe's bunch should be in that building. Hopefully you'll be able to get some kind of clue to the journal's location from them. It's a unique artifact, so you can expect them to defend the secret vigorously.
That's no lie--I'm detecting a surprisingly intricate maze of locks on that floor. It seems they've got something they don't want anyone else getting--could it be the journal?

done.say: Huh, a dead end with lots of guards. Maybe there's something hidden in that room.
Hey! I'm reading some hot code in that desk. See what it is.

Well well, what have we here? Let me hook into that... Ooh, a 1024-bit encrypted code key. Those usually open more interesting things than your normal everyday door key. Let me ping the Machines to do a trace for the lock it fits. Meanwhile, get outside: you're all done in there.

phase.briefing: Their encryption was impressive, for human work: it took us fully 3512.36 milliseconds to decode it. The encryption key has been traced. Enhanced scan of the target area detects the presence of Morpheus' custom paper code. The location is uploading to you now. Proceed there directly and secure the journal.

enter.say: The Machines have already used the key code they decrypted to give you access to the entrance to the secured area. It's up to you to get in there and nab the journal. We only have one chance at this, so let's do it right.

done.say: Uh-oh! That alarm means trouble. You'd better work fast.
Bingo! That Journal's component code is a match for the paper you found in Morpheus' apartment. It's got to be Morpheus'. Grab it and get out of there!
Head outside pronto. The Machines are going to tell us what they want us to do with the journal.

phase.briefing: Surveillance indicates that Niobe's group already has powerful operatives combing the City for you. They must not recapture the journal. Make your way immediately to our stronghold at the indicated coordinates. There you will hand the journal over to our Agents for analysis.

enter.say: What? You're telling me that Morpheus wrote that he wasn't sure about finding the One? I knew you wouldn't be able to resist peeking into that journal of his. You'd better not let the Machines catch you at that. You're supposed to hand it over to Agent Marks, somewhere in that building. I suggest you skip the reading and just hand the journal over ASAP--way too many people would kill you to get that thing.

talk.say: Wait, wait--you're telling me that Morpheus was writing about giving up on the whole "One" thing after his earlier recruit was killed? Wow, who'd have ever thought that? Everyone always talked about how inspiring Morpheus was, how sure of himself-- oopsie, there's Agent Marks. Don't let him catch you reading that thing.
Human. You have the artifact. I will take it. Now.

objective.text: Give the journal to Agent Marks

done.say: Well, I guess that's that. So Morpheus was in a big-time funk for a while there, eh? The big man himself on the verge of despair. I guess that just goes to show, even legends can have their bad days. Anyway, you'd better clear out before Agent Marks gets ticked.
Scanning... Code match found. Article is genuine. Very well {player}, you may leave. Now.

mission.finish: Initial analysis indicates a 99.7% chance that the journal you retrieved is indeed the work of Morpheus. None of the handwritten notes speak of anyone who may have had a motive to assassinate him, aside from us, but we have found that humans often hide their meanings in obscure references. Cross-referencing Morpheus' journal entries against our library of surviving human writings will take some time. In any event, {player}, we appreciate your reliability in this matter. Good day.
